statements.text: Alcohol is a known teratogen with fetal neurodevelopmental risks tied to exposure timing/amount.
statements.explain: Correct. Clinic staff are right that alcohol is a known teratogen with fetal neurodevelopmental risks tied to exposure timing/amount—directly relevant to this client’s drinking.

statements.text: Twin heritability findings do not imply parenting or prenatal environment are irrelevant for individuals.
statements.explain: Correct. A relative’s “twins prove parenting never matters” overreads twin heritability; prenatal environment and parenting can still matter for individuals.

statements.text: If a trait is heritable at all, teratogen advice is scientifically meaningless.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Any heritability does not make teratogen advice scientifically meaningless—exactly the dangerous slogan this clinic must reject.

statements.text: Sensitive periods mean some exposures matter more at certain developmental windows.
statements.explain: Correct. Sensitive periods mean some exposures (like heavy prenatal alcohol) matter more in certain windows—supporting timed counseling for this client.

4.scenario: Night-shift nurses call candy “drive reduction for willpower glucose.” A health psychologist points to stress cues and intermittent reinforcement of snacking; an emotion researcher notes labeling stress as “need sugar.” Performance varies when arousal is labeled threat vs challenge before a simulation.

statements.text: Habit cues and reinforcement can maintain snacking beyond a simple emptied-glucose drive slogan.
statements.explain: Correct. Night-shift nurses call candy “drive reduction for willpower glucose,” but habit cues and intermittent reinforcement of snacking can maintain eating beyond a simple emptied-glucose slogan—as the health psychologist notes.

statements.text: Appraisal of arousal as threat vs challenge can relate to different performance patterns.
statements.explain: Correct. Performance varies when arousal before simulation is labeled threat vs challenge—appraisal differences that an emotion researcher would flag beyond candy-glucose talk.

statements.text: Drive-reduction slogans uniquely explain all human eating under stress with no role for learning.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Drive-reduction slogans do not uniquely explain all stress eating with no role for learning; this ward’s snacking contingencies matter.

statements.text: Affect labeling and contingency awareness can be part of changing coping responses.
statements.explain: Correct. Affect labeling (“need sugar”) and contingency awareness can be part of changing coping—moving beyond the glucose-willpower slogan.

statements.text: Variable-ratio candy wins at work cannot influence behavior when cortisol is high.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Variable-ratio candy wins at work can still influence behavior when cortisol is high; stress does not magically cancel reinforcement.

4.scenario: After a breakup, Sam forecasts permanent misery (affective forecasting error) and rehearses “I’ll never recover” nightly (fluent retrieval of a bleak prediction). Friends suggest behavioral activation and evidence-gathering rather than prophecy rehearsal. Sam cites current dysphoria as perfect future data.

statements.text: People often mis-predict future emotional intensity/duration.
statements.explain: Correct. After the breakup Sam forecasts permanent misery—affective forecasting often mis-predicts intensity/duration of future feelings.

statements.text: Fluent rehearsal of bleak forecasts can increase their subjective believability without proving accuracy.
statements.explain: Correct. Nightly rehearsal of “I’ll never recover” fluently retrieves a bleak prediction, raising its subjective believability without proving accuracy.

statements.text: Behavioral activation and checking evidence can counteract withdrawal that maintains dysphoria.
statements.explain: Correct. Friends’ behavioral activation and evidence-gathering can counteract withdrawal that maintains dysphoria better than prophecy rehearsal.

statements.text: Current mood is an infallible crystal ball for multi-year outcomes, so forecasting research is irrelevant.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Treating current dysphoria as a perfect multi-year crystal ball dismisses forecasting research and locks Sam into the error.

statements.text: Retrieval practice of doom predictions is desirable difficulty that reliably builds optimistic explanatory style.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Retrieval practice of doom predictions is not desirable difficulty that builds optimistic explanatory style—it rehearses the bleak forecast friends are trying to interrupt.

4.scenario: HR wants a 10-item Facebook Big Five quiz to reject “low agreeableness” nursing applicants. I-O and personality psychologists cite reliability/validity and job analysis. A manager says traits beat structured interviews always.

statements.text: Unvalidated viral quizzes lack the psychometric evidence needed for high-stakes hiring.
statements.explain: Correct. HR’s 10-item Facebook Big Five quiz lacks psychometric evidence needed for high-stakes nursing hiring—I-O psychologists cite reliability/validity gaps.

statements.text: Job-related structured interviews/work samples often have stronger validity evidence than informal trait cut scores from social media.
statements.explain: Correct. Job-related structured interviews/work samples often have stronger validity evidence than informal trait cut scores from social-media quizzes for these applicants.

statements.text: Agreeableness cut scores from 10 meme items are automatically content-valid for all nursing tasks.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Agreeableness cut scores from 10 meme items are not automatically content-valid for all nursing tasks.

statements.text: Personality can inform fit but must meet reliability/validity/fairness scrutiny in selection.
statements.explain: Correct. Personality can inform fit but must meet reliability, validity, and fairness scrutiny in selection—unlike the manager’s “traits beat structured interviews always.”.

statements.text: If a quiz is popular, adverse impact and validity concerns disappear legally and scientifically.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Quiz popularity does not erase adverse-impact or validity concerns legally or scientifically for rejecting “low agreeableness” applicants.

4.scenario: A school runs self-esteem week plus tutoring and sleep workshops the same month; grades rise. Rogers-inspired posters get the credit. Motivation data show mastery goals rose mainly in tutored students. Methods teachers cough “confound.”

statements.text: Simultaneous interventions confound causal credit to self-esteem week alone.
statements.explain: Correct. Self-esteem week ran the same month as tutoring and sleep workshops while grades rose—simultaneous interventions confound causal credit to Rogers-inspired posters alone.

statements.text: Tutoring and sleep support are plausible drivers of grade changes.
statements.explain: Correct. Tutoring and sleep workshops ran the same month as self-esteem week while grades rose—so those supports are plausible drivers of the grade change, not only Rogers-inspired posters.

statements.text: Mastery-goal shifts concentrated in tutored students weaken the posters-only story.
statements.explain: Correct. Mastery-goal shifts concentrated in tutored students weaken the posters-only story methods teachers are coughing about.

statements.text: Unconditional positive regard posters are sufficient to prove causation of grade rises even without tutoring.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Unconditional-positive-regard posters alone do not prove causation of grade rises when tutoring co-occurred.

statements.text: Humanistic climate can be helpful for rapport but does not automatically license monocausal credit in confounded rollouts.
statements.explain: Correct. Humanistic climate can help rapport but does not automatically license monocausal credit in this confounded rollout.

4.scenario: A teen explores identity by rejecting a parent’s political club. Parent calls it authoritarian-obedience failure and low conscientiousness; cites peer conformity as proof of no real self. A developmentalist discusses exploration/commitment and social influence without erasing agency.

statements.text: Identity development can include questioning inherited values.
statements.explain: Correct. The teen rejects a parent’s political club while exploring identity—questioning inherited values can be part of identity development, not merely “obedience failure.”.

statements.text: Peer influence is real but does not reduce identity work to “no self.”
statements.explain: Correct. Peer influence is real but does not reduce identity work to “no real self,” as the parent claimed.

statements.text: Authoritarian obedience is not the same construct as healthy identity achievement.
statements.explain: Correct. Authoritarian obedience is not the same construct as healthy identity achievement—the parent’s framing conflates them.

statements.text: Asch-like conformity means teens are incapable of principled reasoning in all domains.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Asch-like conformity does not mean teens are incapable of principled reasoning in all domains—overgeneralizing social influence.

statements.text: Trait labels alone, without developmental context, poorly explain a single political disagreement.
statements.explain: Correct. Slapping “low conscientiousness” on a single political disagreement, without developmental context, poorly explains the teen’s exploration.

4.scenario: Bike-arousal then rating a neutral person as hotter (excitation transfer). Student A: James–Lange means arousal is attraction. Student B: Cannon–Bard forbids misattribution. Student C: two-factor/misattribution fits better.

statements.text: Residual arousal can be misattributed to a salient social target.
statements.explain: Correct. After bike arousal, rating a neutral person as hotter illustrates residual arousal misattributed to a salient social target—excitation transfer.

statements.text: Equating raw arousal with the emotion of attraction without appraisal oversimplifies James–Lange-style teaching debates.
statements.explain: Correct. Student A’s “James–Lange means arousal is attraction” equates raw arousal with the emotion without appraisal—oversimplifying relative to Student C’s two-factor/misattribution fit.

statements.text: Cannon–Bard does not magically make misattribution experiments impossible.
statements.explain: Correct. Student B says Cannon–Bard forbids misattribution; Cannon–Bard does not magically make misattribution experiments like this bike-then-rating case impossible.

statements.text: NMJ dopamine stores attraction engrams during bike pedaling, replacing cognitive labels.
statements.explain: Incorrect. NMJ dopamine storing attraction engrams during pedaling does not replace cognitive labels in this paradigm.

statements.text: Two-factor-style ideas highlight arousal + cognitive interpretation.
statements.explain: Correct. Two-factor-style ideas (arousal + cognitive interpretation) fit Student C’s reading of why the neutral person seems hotter after biking.

4.scenario: A pop reel says childhood “anal stage” explains email hoarding. Records show anxiety after job loss, family modeling of saving, high conscientiousness/scrupulosity. Clinician prefers multi-factor formulation.

statements.text: Unverifiable stage slogans are weak as sole explanations compared with anxiety, modeling, and traits.
statements.explain: Correct. The pop reel’s “anal stage” email-hoarding slogan is a weak sole explanation next to anxiety after job loss, family modeling of saving, and high conscientiousness/scrupulosity in the records.

statements.text: Stressors like job loss can exacerbate saving/hoarding-like behaviors.
statements.explain: Correct. Job-loss anxiety can exacerbate saving/hoarding-like email behavior—more actionable than the Freudian reel.

statements.text: Family modeling is a plausible learning contribution.
statements.explain: Correct. Family modeling of saving is a plausible learning contribution the clinician’s multi-factor formulation should include.

statements.text: A TikTok Freudian label is sufficient assessment with DSM reliability.
statements.explain: Incorrect. A TikTok Freudian label is not sufficient assessment with DSM reliability for this client’s email hoarding.

statements.text: Trait scrupulosity/anxiety themes can inform CBT targets better than reel destiny talk.
statements.explain: Correct. Trait scrupulosity/anxiety themes can inform CBT targets better than reel destiny talk about childhood stages.

4.scenario: All of the following slogans are wrong: genes seal attachment at birth without caregivers; Maslow proved leaderboards always raise intrinsic mentoring; grit posters extinguish unpredictable punishment effects; display rules mean infants show no emotion; neuroticism scores forbid any coping skill learning.

statements.text: Genes seal attachment at birth with no role for caregivers.
statements.explain: Incorrect. The slogan “genes seal attachment at birth without caregivers” denies the caregiving history central to attachment. Caregiver responsiveness is not optional decoration on a genetic seal.

statements.text: Maslow proved public leaderboards always increase intrinsic mentoring.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Maslow did not prove public leaderboards always raise intrinsic mentoring. Extrinsic leaderboards can undermine intrinsic motives—so this slogan fails as a motivation claim.

statements.text: Grit posters extinguish effects of unpredictable punishment without contingency change.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Grit posters do not extinguish effects of unpredictable punishment without changing contingencies. Posters alone do not rewrite operant schedules.

statements.text: Display rules mean infants show no emotion.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Display rules are cultural norms about emotional expression; they do not mean infants show no emotion. That slogan misdefines display rules.

statements.text: Neuroticism forbids learning coping skills.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Neuroticism scores do not forbid learning coping skills. Traits describe tendencies; they are not absolute bans on skill acquisition.

4.scenario: Only this claim is solid for a midterm: secure-base behavior and reunion responses are more informative for attachment than counting cries alone. The distractors are absolute myths.

statements.text: Secure-base use and reunion patterns inform attachment assessment more than cry counts alone.
statements.explain: Correct. Secure-base use and reunion patterns inform attachment assessment more than cry counts alone—the solid midterm claim among the myth distractors.

statements.text: Piaget’s formal operations begin prenatally when teratogens are absent.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Piaget’s formal operations do not begin prenatally when teratogens are absent. That distractor misplaces formal operations far before their developmental window.

statements.text: Drive reduction uniquely explains human art motivation with zero cognition.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Drive reduction does not uniquely explain human art motivation with zero cognition. Art motives involve more than emptied drives.

statements.text: Big Five traits are measured only by inkblots in modern I-O selection.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Big Five traits are not measured only by inkblots in modern I-O selection. That confuses projective lore with contemporary trait assessment.

statements.text: Identity achievement requires total isolation from peers forever.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Identity achievement does not require total isolation from peers forever. Exploration and commitment happen in social contexts, not mandatory solitude.

5.scenario: After a viral CEO scandal montage, employees rate a quiet new manager as unethical (availability + representativeness + FAE). HR has rumor-level data. A consultant urges base rates and situational constraints. Break-room gossip cites “once a cheat, always.”

statements.text: Salient scandals can bias person perception via availability.
statements.explain: Correct. After a viral CEO scandal montage, employees rate a quiet new manager as unethical—salient scandals biasing person perception via availability.

statements.text: Prototype matching can ignore base rates of managerial honesty.
statements.explain: Correct. Matching the new manager to a “cheat” prototype can ignore base rates of managerial honesty HR actually has only at rumor level.

statements.text: Fundamental attribution error themes appear when character is overweighted vs situation.
statements.explain: Correct. Employees overweight the quiet new manager’s character versus situational constraints after the CEO scandal montage—FAE themes the consultant is pushing back on with base rates.

statements.text: Rumor-level data are enough for decisive character causation claims.
statements.explain: Incorrect. HR only has rumor-level data, which is not enough for decisive character-causation claims that the quiet new manager is unethical like the viral CEO.

statements.text: Base-rate and situational information are rational correctives to prototype gossip.
statements.explain: Correct. Base-rate and situational information are rational correctives to break-room gossip that “once a cheat, always” after the scandal montage.

5.scenario: A crowded hallway: student collapses; many stare (pluralistic ignorance / diffusion). Later a witness “remembers” someone helped first (reconstruction). Exam stress is high. RA training is redesigned.

statements.text: Diffusion of responsibility can reduce helping as group size increases.
statements.explain: Correct. In the crowded hallway many stare as a student collapses—diffusion of responsibility can reduce helping as group size increases.

statements.text: Pluralistic ignorance can lead people to interpret nonresponse as a cue that help isn’t needed.
statements.explain: Correct. Pluralistic ignorance can lead bystanders to read others’ nonresponse as a cue that help isn’t needed—fitting the staring crowd.

statements.text: Memory after the fact can reconstruct helpers who didn’t act.
statements.explain: Correct. A later witness “remembering” someone helped first shows reconstructive memory after the collapse, not a perfect recording.

statements.text: Stress always increases helping via broaden-and-build, so training is unnecessary.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Exam stress does not always increase helping via broaden-and-build; redesigning RA training is still warranted.

statements.text: Training that assigns responsibility and concrete steps can improve bystander intervention.
statements.explain: Correct. Training that assigns responsibility and concrete steps can improve bystander intervention—why the RA program is being redesigned.

5.scenario: Call center pays only for call count; mentoring collapses; complaints rise. Managers quote Theory Y posters while punishing “wasted” coaching time. I-O and learning analyses focus on contingencies.

statements.text: Outcome-only incentives can distort behavior toward speed over quality and citizenship.
statements.explain: Correct. Paying only for call count predicts speed over quality and mentoring citizenship—outcome-only incentives distort the call-center climate.

statements.text: Punishing mentoring while rewarding count predicts less mentoring.
statements.explain: Correct. Managers punish “wasted” coaching time while Theory Y posters hang—punishing mentoring while rewarding count predicts less mentoring.

statements.text: Theory Y posters override pay contingencies automatically.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Theory Y posters hanging in the call center do not automatically override pay contingencies that punish “wasted” coaching time while rewarding call count.

statements.text: Aligning rewards with quality and helping can reshape climate more than slogans alone.
statements.explain: Correct. Aligning rewards with quality and helping can reshape climate more than slogans alone—I-O/learning focus on contingencies.

statements.text: Diffusion of responsibility is the sole possible explanation, so incentives are irrelevant.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Diffusion of responsibility is not the sole explanation here; incentive design is directly relevant to mentoring collapse.

5.scenario: Mayor cites SRRS-style talking points after one viral illness story to claim traffic noise alone causes all hypertension, ignoring poverty, heat, and clinic access confounds. Availability is high in speeches.

statements.text: Ecological correlations with confounds cannot isolate noise as sole cause.
statements.explain: Correct. The mayor’s SRRS-style claim that traffic noise alone causes all hypertension ignores poverty, heat, and clinic access—ecological correlations with confounds cannot isolate noise as sole cause.

statements.text: Vivid cases inflate availability of a monocausal story.
statements.explain: Correct. One viral illness story keeps availability high in the mayor’s speeches, inflating a monocausal “traffic noise causes all hypertension” narrative.

statements.text: Poverty and healthcare access are plausible third variables for stress/health links.
statements.explain: Correct. Poverty and healthcare access are plausible third variables for stress/health links the mayor’s noise-only claim skips.

statements.text: SRRS checklist points are experimental manipulations proving causation by themselves.
statements.explain: Incorrect. The mayor’s SRRS-style talking points after one viral illness story are not experimental manipulations that prove traffic noise alone causes all hypertension. Checklist-style stress talk plus an anecdote still leaves poverty, heat, and clinic access confounded.

statements.text: Policy claims need better causal designs than a single correlation + viral anecdote.
statements.explain: Correct. Policy claims that noise alone causes all hypertension need better causal designs than the mayor’s SRRS talking points plus a single viral anecdote.

5.scenario: Elevator panic: CS–US panic pairing then avoidance maintained by relief (negative reinforcement). Work stress raises arousal. Friend recommends cathartic “one big scare.” Clinician plans graded exposure with response prevention.

statements.text: Avoidance can be maintained by negative reinforcement (relief).
statements.explain: Correct. After CS–US panic pairing, elevator avoidance maintained by relief is negative reinforcement—the friend’s “one big scare” plan misses this maintenance process.

statements.text: Exposure/extinction logic targets learned fear more than catharsis theater.
statements.explain: Correct. The clinician’s graded exposure with response prevention targets learned fear via extinction logic better than cathartic theater.

statements.text: Cathartic re-traumatization is the gold-standard mandatory first step for every phobia.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Cathartic re-traumatization is not the gold-standard mandatory first step for every phobia—contrary to the friend’s advice.

statements.text: Stress can potentiate anxiety responding without rewriting the learning account of avoidance.
statements.explain: Correct. Work stress raising arousal can potentiate anxiety without rewriting the learning account of elevator avoidance.

statements.text: If classical acquisition occurred, operant avoidance maintenance is logically impossible.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Classical acquisition of panic does not make operant avoidance maintenance logically impossible—both stages appear in this elevator case.

5.scenario: Depression: anhedonia, mood-congruent recall, “I’ll always fail” schema, night-shift sleep collapse. Friends push forced gratitude only. Care team discusses CBT/BA, sleep, and possible meds without shame.

statements.text: Cognitive schemas and mood-congruent memory can maintain depressive outlook.
statements.explain: Correct. Anhedonia, mood-congruent recall, and “I’ll always fail” schemas can maintain depressive outlook—friends’ gratitude-only push doesn’t address these mechanisms.

statements.text: Sleep disruption can worsen mood regulation.
statements.explain: Correct. This client’s night-shift sleep collapse can worsen mood regulation alongside anhedonia and “I’ll always fail” schemas—sleep is part of the care picture, not a side note.

statements.text: Forced gratitude alone rarely replaces structured depression care.
statements.explain: Correct. Forced gratitude alone rarely replaces structured CBT/BA and related depression care the team is discussing.

statements.text: Anhedonia means success memories were never encoded, so BA cannot help.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Anhedonia does not mean success memories were never encoded so BA cannot help—BA remains a plausible psychosocial option.

statements.text: Combined psychosocial and biomedical options can be appropriate depending on severity.
statements.explain: Correct. Combined psychosocial and biomedical options can be appropriate depending on severity—without the shame framing friends implied.

5.scenario: PTSD survivor: intrusions, avoidance, hypervigilance. Forums urge hypnosis to “erase the tape.” Legal interviewers risk leading questions. Clinician protects against suggestion while offering evidence-based trauma care and sleep support.

statements.text: Trauma memories are not literal erasable videotapes.
statements.explain: Correct. Forums urge hypnosis to “erase the tape,” but trauma memories are not literal erasable videotapes for this PTSD survivor.

statements.text: Leading questions risk contaminating reports (misinformation).
statements.explain: Correct. Legal interviewers’ leading questions risk contaminating reports via misinformation—clinician caution is warranted.

statements.text: Evidence-based trauma therapies exist that don’t rely on erase-the-tape hypnosis myths.
statements.explain: Correct. Evidence-based trauma therapies exist that don’t rely on erase-the-tape hypnosis myths, alongside sleep support.

statements.text: Hypnosis guarantees deletion of episodic trauma without suggestion risk.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Hypnosis does not guarantee deletion of episodic trauma without suggestion risk—the forum promise is unsafe mythology.

statements.text: Avoidance can be reinforced by short-term anxiety reduction, maintaining PTSD cycles.
statements.explain: Correct. Avoidance can be reinforced by short-term anxiety reduction, maintaining PTSD symptom cycles the clinician is treating.

5.scenario: Rural client stops antidepressants after TikTok stigma (“meds = weakness”), sleep crashes, depression worsens. Barriers to care are high. Plan: stigma counseling, telehealth CBT, collaborative med education, safety planning.

statements.text: Stigma is a real barrier to treatment utilization.
statements.explain: Correct. Stopping antidepressants after TikTok “meds = weakness” stigma shows stigma as a real barrier to treatment utilization for this rural client.

statements.text: Abrupt medication changes and sleep loss can worsen clinical status—coordinate care.
statements.explain: Correct. Abrupt medication changes plus sleep crash and worsening depression call for coordinated care, not solo TikTok decisions.

statements.text: Telehealth can reduce some access barriers when available.
statements.explain: Correct. Telehealth CBT in the plan can reduce some access barriers when rural in-person care is hard.

statements.text: Stigma posts prove medications are never appropriate for depression.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Stigma posts do not prove medications are never appropriate for depression—the collaborative med education piece of the plan rejects that.

statements.text: Psychosocial and biomedical tools can be integrated rather than framed as mutually exclusive morality.
statements.explain: Correct. Psychosocial and biomedical tools can be integrated rather than framed as mutually exclusive morality (“weakness”).

5.scenario: Hospital replaces ERP for OCD with “energy tapping” based on testimonials (availability) after a morale boost during rollout (attention effects). Methods psychologist demands outcome evidence before dropping exposure.

statements.text: Testimonials are weak efficacy evidence compared with controlled outcome studies.
statements.explain: Correct. Replacing ERP for OCD with energy tapping based on testimonials is weak efficacy evidence compared with controlled outcome studies the methods psychologist demands.

statements.text: Transient morale/attention effects can mimic early improvement without durable specific efficacy.
statements.explain: Correct. Morale boost during rollout can create attention effects that mimic early improvement without durable specific efficacy for tapping.

statements.text: ERP/exposure-based care has a stronger evidence tradition for OCD than energy tapping testimonials.
statements.explain: Correct. ERP/exposure-based care has a stronger evidence tradition for OCD than the energy-tapping testimonials that replaced it after the hospital’s morale-boost rollout.

statements.text: Availability of emotional stories outranks RCTs for deciding first-line OCD care.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Availability of emotional stories should not outrank RCTs when deciding first-line OCD care in this hospital.

statements.text: Mechanism vagueness does not make tapping superior to extinction-based approaches.
statements.explain: Correct. Vague “energy” mechanisms do not make tapping superior to extinction-based ERP the hospital is dropping.

5.scenario: Online pile-on: likes reinforce harsher posts (VR), outrage videos leave residual arousal that transfers to new targets, moderators blame “true aggressive personality only.” Policy debate on redesigning contingencies.

statements.text: Intermittent social rewards can escalate aggressive posting.
statements.explain: Correct. Likes reinforcing harsher posts can escalate aggressive posting via intermittent social rewards (variable-ratio style).

statements.text: Residual arousal can amplify aggressive responses to new targets.
statements.explain: Correct. Outrage videos leaving residual arousal that transfers to new targets fits excitation-transfer amplification of aggression.

statements.text: Platform design contingencies are intervention points beyond trait fatalism.
statements.explain: Correct. Moderators blaming “true aggressive personality only” miss platform design contingencies as intervention points.

statements.text: Variable-ratio likes extinguish posting by definition, so reinforcement cannot explain escalation.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Variable-ratio likes do not extinguish posting by definition—they maintain/escalate it, which is why reinforcement explains the pile-on.

statements.text: Trait explanations can coexist with situational amplifiers—but traits alone rarely excuse ignoring contingencies.
statements.explain: Correct. Traits can coexist with situational amplifiers, but trait fatalism alone rarely excuses ignoring like/outrage contingencies in policy redesign.

5.scenario: Every statement here is a clinical/social myth trap: bystander effect means larger crowds always help more; Type A hostility is unrelated to health research themes; SSRIs prove therapy is useless; graphology is gold-standard leadership selection; obedience research implies modern authority cues never influence harm-doing.

statements.text: Bystander effect means larger crowds always help more.
statements.explain: Incorrect. The myth list says the bystander effect means larger crowds always help more. Bystander research typically warns that larger groups can reduce helping via diffusion—not guarantee more help.

statements.text: Hostility components in Type A research were never linked to health discussions.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Hostility components in Type A research have been discussed in health psychology; saying they were “never linked” is a myth trap on this list.

statements.text: SSRIs prove psychotherapy is useless for all conditions.
statements.explain: Incorrect. SSRIs do not prove psychotherapy is useless for all conditions. Medication evidence does not erase psychosocial care across disorders.

statements.text: Graphology is a gold-standard, validated leadership selection tool.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Graphology is not a gold-standard validated leadership selection tool. Handwriting analysis lacks the validity this myth claims.

statements.text: Modern authority cues never influence harm-doing because classic obedience work failed to replicate at 100%.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Even if classic obedience work did not replicate at 100%, modern authority cues can still influence harm-doing. Non-perfect replication does not zero out authority effects.

5.scenario: Keep only the accurate public-health persuasion claim: fear appeals about binge drinking work better when paired with specific, credible response-efficacy steps; fear alone can trigger reactance or denial.

statements.text: Fear plus clear efficacy/action steps is generally wiser than fear-only messaging.
statements.explain: Correct. For binge-drinking fear appeals, pairing fear with specific, credible response-efficacy steps is generally wiser than fear alone, which can trigger reactance or denial—the accurate public-health claim to keep.

statements.text: Maximum fear without efficacy advice is always optimal for every audience.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Maximum fear without efficacy advice is not always optimal for every audience. Fear-only binge-drinking messages can backfire without actionable steps.

statements.text: Reactance never occurs in health campaigns.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Reactance can occur in health campaigns; denying reactance is a trap next to the fear-plus-efficacy keeper.

statements.text: Celebrity liking is definitionally central-route processing of vaccine statistics.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Celebrity liking is typically peripheral-route persuasion, not definitionally central-route processing of vaccine statistics. That distractor mislabels ELM routes.

statements.text: Optimistic bias means no health message can ever influence anyone, so drop efficacy content.
statements.explain: Incorrect. Optimistic bias does not mean no health message can ever influence anyone. Dropping efficacy content because of bias would undermine the fear-plus-efficacy approach this item keeps.
